payload.objective: Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of CYBB-p.His101Arg (CYBB, UniProt P04839) and test it with one targeted computational test.
payload.question: For a pathogenic missense variant in an immune-deficiency gene, which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function, and does a targeted computational test change the conclusion that the starting evidence suggested?

payload.statement: ClinVar classifies NM_000397.4(CYBB):c.302A>G (p.His101Arg) as Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts; 4 submissions) for X-linked chronic granulomatous disease.
payload.strength: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts (2 of 4 stars)

payload.statement: UniProtKB annotates residue 101 of P04839 as a Binding site: axial binding residue (ligand heme b, CHEBI:60344), supported by experimental evidence.
UniProtKB natural variant VAR_002432 at residue 101 (H to R) is annotated as the cause of X-linked chronic granulomatous disease (CGDX).
AlphaMissense gives p.His101Arg of P04839 a pathogenicity score of 0.9975, classed as likely pathogenic.
payload.strength: computational prediction, not validated for clinical use (0.9975 on 0-1 scale)

payload.statement: Five experimental cryo-EM structures of P04839 observe residue 101; none carries a mutation at that residue, and the ligands across them include HEM in all five.
Cryo-EM structure 8X2L (2.99 Å) of human phagocyte NADPH oxidase observes residue 101 with ligands HEM, MG, NAG, FAD.
UniProtKB function: CYBB is the catalytic subunit of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase, transferring electrons from NADPH via FAD and two heme molecules to O2 to make superoxide.
Residue 101 lies in the predicted transmembrane helix spanning residues 96 to 130 of P04839.
No PubMed literature was returned by Europe PMC for CYBB p.His101Arg or His101Arg.
payload.why_it_matters: Without a paper measuring the H101R mutant, the mechanism rests on annotation and predictions rather than measured heme binding or superoxide output.

payload.statement: A 2022 Nature Communications cryo-EM study of the core NOX2 heterodimer states that mutations causing NOX2 deficiency correlate with chronic granulomatous disease.
A 1998 study identified CYBB mutations responsible for X-linked chronic granulomatous disease in 131 kindreds, describing the gp91-phox component as the site of these defects.
No retrieved source measures heme incorporation, superoxide output or p22phox binding for the H101R mutant specifically.
payload.why_it_matters: The three mechanism classes (heme ligand loss, folding destabilisation, p22phox interface loss) differ only in these measurements, so they cannot be ranked by literature alone.

payload.statement: H101R removes the axial histidine that coordinates the heme b iron in the transmembrane core of gp91phox (CYBB). Without this ligand the heme cannot be stably incorporated, so electron transfer from FAD to O2 fails and superoxide output is lost.
payload.would_refute: The variant residue is not within contact distance of the HEM ligand in experimental structures, or the structure-based test shows the arginine side chain is accommodated in the heme pocket with no loss of heme contact.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: UniProtKB annotates residue 101 as the axial heme b binding residue on experimental evidence, and five cryo-EM structures carry HEM. Pathogenic ClinVar and CGDX annotations are consistent with loss of function.

payload.statement: H101R destabilises the transmembrane helix spanning residues 96 to 130 by placing a charged arginine in the membrane core, so the folding free energy falls, the protein is misfolded or degraded, and the oxidase is lost without a specific ligand defect.
payload.would_refute: The predicted folding free-energy change of H101R is near zero or stabilising, so the substitution does not destabilise the fold.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: High AlphaMissense (0.9975), EVE pathogenic class and residue placement within a predicted helix support a folding effect, but no measured stability datum exists yet, so it ranks below the heme-ligand annotation.

payload.statement: H101R disrupts the heterodimer interface between gp91phox (CYBB) and the p22phox subunit (CYBA) in the transmembrane region, so the core cytochrome b558 cannot assemble and the catalytic subunit is not stably held in the membrane.
payload.would_refute: The structure comparison or the ligand-free pocket and interface analysis shows residue 101 is outside the CYBA contact surface, and the variant does not change the predicted interface.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Core heterodimer with CYBA is documented and residue 101 sits in the membrane helix, but no retrieved source places residue 101 at the p22phox interface, so this is the least supported.

payload.description: Checks whether residue 101 neighbours the HEM ligand in the five experimental cryo-EM structures that observe it. A contact supports H1; no contact in ligand-bound structures would weaken H1.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A contact confirms the favoured hypothesis; absence of contact would refute H1 and reorder the ranking toward H2. It does not discriminate H2 from H3.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: The tool reports can_run true with 5 structures observing residue 101 and holding non-solvent ligands; zero compute seconds.
controls: Negative control: ligands in the same structures that never list the residue as a neighbour.
Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.
Site-state control: structures in which the residue itself is mutated are reported separately.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change of H101R on the AlphaFold model. A destabilising value supports H2; a neutral value weakens H2 but says nothing about heme binding.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: Separates H2 from H1, since H1 predicts no stability change; but FoldX error is near 1 kcal/mol and the result may not reorder H1 unless neutral.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: Tool reports FoldX state ok; zero compute seconds.
controls: Within-site comparison: the same predictor for the other substitutions reported at this residue.
Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: Predicted pocket and predicted interface membership of residue 101 on the AlphaFold model (P2Rank and ProtVar). Pocket membership weakly supports H1; interface membership would support H3.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: Interface data for this residue is not covered (ProtVar interface state not_covered), so a null result would be uninformative for H3; pocket result is only weak support.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: Runs on the AlphaFold model with P2Rank, but ProtVar interface coverage is not_covered for this residue.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.
Confidence control: mean pLDDT of the pocket residues.

payload.rationale: T1 tests the top-ranked mechanism (H1, heme axial ligand loss) directly against experimental structures, costs zero compute seconds, needs no approval, and can refute H1 if residue 101 does not neighbour HEM. T2 would test H2 but FoldX error near 1 kcal/mol limits what a neutral result shows. T3 has poor interface coverage for this residue. Structure comparison is not runnable because ESM Atlas did not answer.

rejected.reason: Tests H2 with a computational predictor whose error is near 1 kcal/mol; the favoured H1 is more directly testable now at zero cost.
ProtVar interface coverage for residue 101 is not_covered, so a null result would not refute H3; pocket result is only weak evidence for H1.

payload.findings: review_claims checked 19 statements: no clinical or treatment wording, no evidence items without a source, and all 3 hypotheses carry the agent-generated label. T1 is a retrieval-only test with no approval requirement and zero compute seconds. Research use only; no clinical interpretation is drawn.

The residue is not contacted by any negative-control ligand, and none of the observing structures carries a mutation at residue 101.

values.headline: Residue 101 is within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 5 of 5 ligand-bound structures (HEM); closest 2.0 Å to HEM (PROTOPORPHYRIN IX CONTAINING FE) in PDB 8GZ3.

per_hypothesis.why: Residue 101 is 2.0 to 2.12 Å from HEM in all five HEM-bound structures, consistent with direct axial coordination of the heme iron; no negative-control ligand contacts the residue.
A ligand contact says nothing about fold stability; no stability value was measured.
The test did not measure protein-protein interface membership; no interface evidence was obtained.

payload.uncertainty: Contact distance is a crystal or cryo-EM geometry measurement in structures that hold the reference residue, not a measurement of the H101R mutant. A 2.0 Å contact is compatible with a histidine axial ligand but does not show heme loss for the arginine. The test does not separate H1 from H2 or H3, and it cannot show that the arginine would fail to bind heme.

payload.why: T1 found residue 101 at 2.0 to 2.12 Å from HEM in 5 of 5 ligand-bound structures [T1], supporting the axial heme ligand annotation [E2]. H1 stays favoured; H2 and H3 are unchanged because T1 did not measure them.

payload.description: Run the stability test (T2) to measure the FoldX folding free-energy change of H101R, which tests H2 directly. Then run the structural context test on the AlphaFold model to check whether residue 101 lies in a predicted interface with CYBA (H3). Outcome to confirm H1: a neutral stability value and no interface membership, leaving heme-ligand loss as the only mechanism the data support. Outcome to overturn it: a destabilising value at or above threshold would move H2 up.
payload.why_now: T1 supports H1 but cannot separate it from H2 or H3, and T2 costs zero compute seconds with no approval required.

## Question
What molecular mechanism best explains loss of function of CYBB p.His101Arg (NOX2 / gp91phox, UniProt P04839), and which single test checks it? This is a research question only; no recommendations are made.

## Evidence
ClinVar classifies NM_000397.4:c.302A>G (p.His101Arg) as Pathogenic with no conflicts [E1]. UniProtKB annotates residue 101 as an axial binding residue for heme b on experimental evidence [E2], and lists the H-to-R change as a natural variant causing X-linked chronic granulomatous disease [E3]. AlphaMissense scores the substitution 0.9975 [E4]. CYBB is the catalytic subunit that passes electrons from FAD through two hemes to O2 [E7], and residue 101 lies in a predicted helix spanning residues 96 to 130 [E8]. A 2022 cryo-EM study links NOX2 deficiency mutations to chronic granulomatous disease [E9]. No literature measuring the H101R mutant was found [G1].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
[H1] (ligand binding, favoured): loss of the axial histidine removes heme b coordination, so electron transfer and superoxide output fail. [H2] (stability): a charged arginine destabilises the transmembrane helix. [H3] (protein interaction): the variant disrupts the CYBA interface. No retrieved source places residue 101 at the CYBA interface [G2].

## Tests considered and the choice
Three tests could run now: ligand contact [T1], stability [T2] and structural context [T3]. Structure comparison was blocked because the ESM Atlas service did not answer. T1 was chosen because it tests the favoured mechanism directly, costs no compute and needs no approval. T2 was rejected because its error is near 1 kcal/mol, and T3 because interface coverage for residue 101 is absent.

## Result
Residue 101 lies within 2.0 to 2.12 Å of HEM in all five ligand-bound structures [T1]. No negative-control ligand contacts the residue [T1].

## Updated decision
H1 remains favoured [T1]. The contact supports axial heme coordination, but H2 and H3 were not measured, so their ranking is unchanged.

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
The contact is measured on the reference residue, not the arginine variant, so it does not show heme loss for H101R. The test cannot separate H1 from H2 or H3. Validation needs the stability test [T2], an interface check, and ideally a measured heme incorporation or superoxide assay on the mutant.

## Next experiment
Run the stability test [T2] to test H2. A neutral value together with no interface membership would leave H1 as the only mechanism the data support. A destabilising value at or above threshold would raise H2.
